COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place; rather, he is compensated for the loss, which he suffered as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34;
Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].

PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 23.

The petitioner (PW1) has placed on record her original medical bills with respect to consultation,
investigation, dressings, medicines, implant costs, etc. for a total sum of Rs.36,121/-, which have been proved on record as Ex.PW1/13 to Ex.PW1/36.

Further, the same have also been found in order.
Hence, a sum of Rs.36,121/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Income During Treatment 24.
The petitioner (PW1) has stated that due to the injuries received in the accident, she had to remain bed ridden from the date of accident on 22.10.2018 till 02.01.2019.

As per Ex.PW1/12, the OPD visit Card of AIIMS, New Delhi, it is found mentioned that the petitioner was on complete bed r e s t t i l l 0 2 . 0 1 . 2 0 1 9 d u e t o e x c e s s i v e b a c k p a i n ____________________________________________________________ and that she started ambulating since 02.01.2019.

Further, she was observed "sensation- impaired from below waist" and she was advised (i) to continue medicine i.e., tablet MGALIN 75 HS; (ii) to continue using spinal brace, (iii) exercise of spinal extension
and she was referred to nearest Govt. District Hospital for Disability Certificate.

25. Considering the above medical record of the petitioner, it may be safely inferred that, due to the above medical condition of the petitioner, she would not have been in a position to resume her work till 02.01.2019 from the date of accident on 22.10.2018.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for the loss of 70 days of income during treatment.

The broad criteria for ascertaining the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity of the injured have been given in case of Raj Kumar (supra).

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said judgment further observed that what requires to be assessed by the Claims Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency).

However, in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that the percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of permanent disability is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation.

That the crucial factor which has to be taken into consideration, as per the Hon'ble Supreme Court, is to assess as to whether the permanent disability has any adverse effect on the earning capacity of the injured.
A person who is engaged and cannot freely move to attend to his duties may not be able to match the earning in comparison with the one who is healthy and bodily abled.

31.
